mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand, which boosts economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where the proxy shows sustained growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals economic weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, which leads to reduced corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month signals growing consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2% each in a month signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.2% and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over a 3-month period signals inflationary pressures, which erodes real returns and increases the cost of capital, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the proxy shows sustained growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% in a quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, which reduces corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.
